reviews.text: 关注挺久了，匆匆玩了一章，可以玩，但是不太推荐，目前还欠打磨，本来可以更加精致的 -做了踩油门的动画但是没有做刹车和挂档的，明明都已经画出来了，就差这一点动画吗 -路上的小故事有点过于碎片、独立，整体体验也是如此，感觉可以做到更加连贯的 -简中在犄角旮旯的位置有一些机翻，无伤大雅，但是剧情里的口口口就有点影响体验了，我搁这做完形填空呢？ -整体感觉上架很仓促，姑且给推荐是因为进去显示0.8的版本号，观望一阵吧 总体评价：我不是很确定睡一觉醒来明天会不会打开这个游戏

很有创意的游戏，将Roguelike、视觉小说和赛车游戏进行结合是一次大胆的尝试。目前首发版玩了一下，整体观感还是不错的。写下这份评测，给后来的中国玩家做个简要参考吧！ 一个人、一辆车、一条大路通天边。这就是一部美式公路片的三要素（我乱说的）。而《Heading Out》（官方译名为《西部公路》，我觉得或许也可以译成更狠一点的活，比如《绝命狂飙》或者《惊梦逃亡》啥的）（也是我乱说的）这一游戏正像是对一部公路旅行片的致敬。连画面都采用了黑白美漫风。 主角是一名车手，他将踏上一场横跨美国的旅途。在路途上，他会遇到许多人，许多事。超速行驶的美式肌肉车横跨美国各州，并在路途上不断引起其他车手和当地警方的注意。随着主角不断前行，他所做出的每一个选择都会影响人们眼中他的形象，是一名除暴安良，仗义行天涯的西部牛仔？还是一名臭名昭著，逃离正义审判的暴徒？主角的声誉和名望都会量化显示在屏幕上，可以随时追踪。游戏也自带提示（可以在设置中调整），这样在事件中做出选择时，可以提前预计不同选择带来的不同后果。 选择与资源管理也是这个游戏很重要的方面，如果钱不够付燃油费、车子状况不佳、乃至人物过于疲惫……种种因素都会对你的旅行造成危害。同时，不要以为只要减速慢行就能躲避一切危机。玩过《极品飞车16》的朋友或许还记得，在《极品飞车16》中，如果在到达检查点时不在规定的名次内，车手就会被淘汰。而在《西部公路》中，主角的恐惧则化为红色的梦魇如影随形，在主角前行时，恐惧值也会如病毒般沿公路蔓延并跟随主角。如果主角在一个地方停留得太久，就会被梦魇赶上并吞噬。 这个游戏可以分成两部分：大地图模式和赛车模式。在大地图模式下，主角需要选择前行的路线，躲避警察的追捕，并且合理规划资源。这一部分就是类Roguelike的玩法。主角需要根据行驶的里程和速度花费金钱加油，要是油钱不够，就只能加霸王油然后被条子追。而随着时间流逝主角的注意力也会逐渐涣散（可参考《欧洲卡车模拟2》的疲劳值）。如果疲劳值过高，主角在赛车时就会打瞌睡（表现为屏幕一黑）。所以，玩家需要规划时间、物品和金钱，避免陷入四面楚歌的境地。当然，有的时候也会遇到警察追捕，或是车手发起挑战。这时就要进入赛车模式，在公路上踩下油门狂飙。这一部分又是赛车游戏的玩法。赛车模式每次只会持续一首歌的时间（约2~3分钟），在赛车时务必注意不要横冲直撞，毕竟车辆耐久也是有限的。一定要注意屏幕侧边显示的路牌标识，它可以告诉你接下来的路况以及哪里有捷径。在保证别一头攮死在树上或者开进沟里的前提下……能开多快就开多快！ 选择前进的路线时，需要谨慎再谨慎。每条路都会带来无法预料的后果，可能是突发险情、可能是警匪追逐、可能是街头赛车……随着驾驶路程的增加，也要记住，资源不是无穷无尽的，时间、精力、金钱、耐久之间应该如何取得平衡？若是经常参加比赛，那么即便能获得更多金钱，车辆的耐久也会损耗更快；假如决定在城市休息一下恢复精力，虽然可以让你免受疲劳驾驶的困扰，却也给了梦魇迎头赶上的机会…… 猛踩油门吧！你能做的就是开车、开车、开得比所有警察、所有车手、所有恐惧都快！ 梳理一下这个游戏的一些优缺点（叠甲：以下纯属个人意见） 优点： 具有鲜明特点的美漫画风 不俗的音乐与剧情沉浸感 就像《极品飞车16》遇上《96号公路》一样精彩 简单又不失策略的物品/金钱/时间管理 缺点： 一开始的剧情让人有点云里雾里 手感和物理跟一般的赛车游戏比起来还是怪怪的，车子总爱扭来扭去 优化不太好，我电脑风扇转得飞起 在简口中文口境下游口口会出现中文口成口块的情口（作为一个需要文字剧情推动的游戏，汉化出问题实在是大败笔） [h3]Note: Developers, if you see this review, please fix Simplified Chinese display error ASAP ![/h3]

None of the screenshots show how the actual gameplay looks like - that you'll be spending time looking at the map, holding RT when the icon of your car moves through the USA. When you get to an encounter, you'll eventually see your car during a race or something. But I thought it's an actual traveling game, not a simulation.

Its advertised as a stylized, roguelike inspired, open-world driving game. It is actually resource management ala oregon trail with interspersed five minute driving sections once or twice per stop. You only catch a glimpse of what the bulk of the gameplay is actually like in the trailers. That gameplay is watching a dot on a map slowly move to event spaces. It's more of a visual novel but marketed as a driving game. The radio is the focal point more than the driving and the radio's focus is on the DJs. The music is phenomenal. No complaints. The DJs play their parts well but the overt political tones stick out. The main narrator is toeing the line between a good grizzled performance and pure cringe. It's a tightrope. Sometimes the dialogue hits and other times I'm laughing at the game. Very cool art style, music and the driving (when there is driving) is pretty good. The script is the weakest aspect which is compounded by the game being very dialogue/text heavy. I mostly enjoy the game and I like the nods to Initial D and other media. I just wish there was more like, racing. Dodging traffic on two lane highways gets stale quickly.

先说结论。 游戏类型：有开车环节的、注重资源管理的剧情驱动文字冒险肉鸽游戏（并非模拟驾驶游戏，游戏更不存在可以互动的开放世界） 优点： 1：不错的驾驶手感，但可能需要手柄才能有良好体验。 2：美漫线条+黑白画面的美术风格非常独特。 3：西部公路逃亡的游戏氛围很好，沉浸感也不错。 4：游戏致敬了一些经典电影，如《粉身碎骨》《亡命驾驶》，能get到的影迷应该会喜欢。 缺点： 1：目前的汉化有些微机翻痕迹，且会随机出现汉字显示成口口口的情况。 2：游戏内容少，可重复游玩度低，深度游玩动力不足。具体来说就是：目前游戏的内容只够支撑一周目的游玩，在一周目通关之后游戏也没有二周目和其他游戏模式可供游玩。游戏内无论是驾驶还是资源管理系统都没有足够的深度值得玩家研究，更没有什么长期目标能够让玩家投入大量时间（追求全成就除外）。对我本人来说，如果不是游戏的开车手感我很喜欢，一周目通关之后我可能都不会再碰这个游戏。 3：首发期游戏老生常谈的bug和优化问题。游戏的优化一般，但也没到不能玩的程度；bug方面目前有人遇到了导致死档的恶性bug，但我本人没有遇到，可能是运气比较好吧。 总体评价：一款能玩，好玩，但是内容少、不耐玩的小品级游戏。但独特的美术风格可能会有点挑人。初见时可能会觉得很不错，但经不起高强度游玩，容易腻，偶尔闲来无事时开一把消磨时间挺好。 购买建议：喜欢游戏氛围和美术风格，且不排斥肉鸽玩法和类视觉小说叙事的玩家可以入手，如果不急着玩可以等一手后期更新或折扣。 ———————————————————————————————————————— 以下是我对这款游戏的驾驶手感和车辆本身的一些看法，不感兴趣的玩家可以不看。 ———————————————————————————————————————— 在公路上的驾驶手感： 1：车辆的抓地力并没有想象中那么高，方向给多了很容易滑。 2：在抓地状态下，游戏的物理可以运行得非常良好，你能明显感受到一种对车辆的操控感，有一种尽在掌握的惬意，这点我很喜欢。 3：轮胎在刚刚开始打滑时还能保持转向能力，一旦形成甩尾便很难救车，只能松开油门小心调整方向等车身慢慢回正，或者拉手刹调整姿态。万万不可继续踩着油门猛地反打方向。同时车子从打滑到甩尾之间在一定程度上缺乏过渡。 4：建议驾驶时小心控制油门和方向，因此手柄的游戏体验要明显优于键盘。 5：游戏通过可以拉手刹来一键漂移，但说是漂移，其实也就是让车辆直接进入上面提过的打滑但不甩尾的状态，过急弯时这样体感会比抓地快一些。虽然同样有着Break to Drift的机制，但在这款游戏里，想做出类似寒霜NFS里长距离漂移的动作基本是不可能的。 在非铺装路面上的驾驶手感： 1：非铺装路面对车辆的降速效果并没有很明显，但本就不高的抓地力会进一步降低，救车也会更难。 2：你可以选择离开公路抄近路，但同时也要在转向上承担更高的风险。 3：必须要给出好评的一点是，当你一侧轮子压上草地，另一侧轮子还留在公路上时，你会明显感受到草地一侧轮胎与公路一侧轮胎的抓地力差异，并且车辆的前进方向会朝草地一侧偏移（这一点和现实中是一样的）。此时如果你不及时调整车身姿态，车辆很有可能会因为这种抓地力差异而失控。 “车”本身： 1：游戏里车辆的仪表盘和内饰做的不错，让我惊喜的一点是居然还把油门和换挡动画做出来了，而且这个油门动画是真的会根据你的扳机力度来播放的。美中不足的是没有做刹车与离合的动作，希望以后可以补上。 2：游戏车辆后部、侧面的车损做的不错，但是车头的车损几乎没有。反正在我和对向车道的街车迎面相撞之后我是没看出来车头有什么变化。 3：游戏中共有4辆可驾驶的车辆，都是缝合车，性能上确实有些区别，但手感大同小异，而且游戏内不存在改装系统。 4：游戏里初始的肌肉车原型是什么我还真没看出来，上世纪美国肌肉车里四幅圆形头灯的设计并不少见，我个人感觉车头更像初代的道奇Challenger，尾灯可能参考了三代道奇Challenger SRT8的设计。 5：游戏里那些和你比赛的车手开的车也都是不一样的，具体我没细看，但是其中有一辆看尾灯貌似是二代Charger R/T 426或二代庞蒂亚克GTO抠掉了尾翼？ 另外，有卡在第四幕最终决战的兄弟，这一关的过关条件并不是超过幽灵车，而是在看到一系列“你”“必须”“转”“身”的路牌时直接调头原路返回，等恐惧条读满就过关了，这反直觉的设计当时也卡了我好一会，还是问了已经通关的朋友才知道原来这一关是这么过的，希望对卡关的朋友有帮助。

[h1]There's something about this... it's hard to explain.[/h1] [i]The game gives you a 3 minute window. However long the song lasts. Anything happens in that 3 minutes and you're him. No matter what. Anything happens a minute either side of that and you're on your own. Do you understand?[/i] Well, if you don't, then ask yourself this: [h2]Do you like Vanishing Point? Perhaps Sin City? Maybe both? Do you drive?[/h2] As long as the answer to either of these questions, the more the merrier, is yes [b]or[/b] you just openly identify as Ryan Gosling (he's literally you, after all), then it's safe to say this game is for you. [b]However[/b], please note that this game is a visual novel/racing game, not just a roadtrip simulator. There's about a 50/50 split when it comes to the actual gameplay [i]and[/i] choosing a route/moving along the map; it's not a map you can just open up while driving, it's a separate element. The trailer definitely does a poor job at pointing this out, so if you think regular pauses between driving sections (the latter of which usually last a whole song, i.e. 3:30 min.), are too immersion-breaking for you, then that is definitely something to consider. Still, I honestly think that including the map the way they did, having to manage aspects like your speed, because it directly affects gas and how much it will cost you, the events you come across, including cop cars you have to react to and stop for (or not!) and all the little scenes when you meet all different kinds of characters, do a lot more good than harm to the story. The latter are voice-narrated, which adds to the game's feel quite a bit, usually prompting you to make a decision as well: [h3]Are you going to sacrifice some money or time, in order to gain some reputation and fame? Perhaps vice-versa?[/h3] [spoiler]While your "fear" keeps creeping up on you[/spoiler], you'll also need to manage things like your "focus" by resting in cities, which might lose you a bit of time, sure, but it'll also make sure that you're fit for the long road ahead. Alternatively, you can take some... uhm... "substances", that's the word! They'll do the trick too. More or less. Last but definitely not least, you obviously have to manage your car's condition as well, which can be damaged by crashing (duh..) in the aforementioned driving sections. That's not gonna happen to you though, remember? You are him!
“I give you five minutes when we get there. Anything happens in that five minutes and I'm yours. No matter what.”

Schizophrenic Ryan Gosling races across the country to escape his fear of something that he is afraid of that he fears and also the other Ryan Gosling. (Game is infinitely more fun when playing on 'challenging' difficulty and setting 'hide consequences' to ON.)
I bought a driving game, got therapy on top of it

整个游戏的推进框架结构就是照着《vanishing point》这部电影来的，最典型的地方就是 ， 1 伴你同行并直播你路途的电台，电影里是个盲人黑人老哥， 2 每次旅程结尾的撞车路障，那个设置，两台推土机两台警车，然后主角直接装上去，这点和电影几乎是一样的， 3 UI的点线地图和电影里警察局标记主角车辆的灯线图是一样的思路， 4 第二幕里出现的传奇车手 ，这个角色的背景和那台1970 Dodge Challenger R/T和电影的主角科瓦茨基的背景故事及座驾都是一样的， 5 当然，游戏玩家的初始车也是同款，只是前脸的进气格栅有所变动，包括玩家的快递员属性，电影里的主角就是为了把车送到目的地才上路的 ， 6 游戏里和警察遭遇基本都是因为超速，这个点 在电影里也是科瓦茨基被警察追了半个美国的初始原因 7 游戏本身呈现的那股南方红脖子在旷野 中西部自由散漫地兜风感觉 以及他们眼中破烂但很阿美莉卡的味道 ，还是很还原电影的 以上几点喜欢 或者能接受 还是很推荐试试的，也可以等个大折扣，但是要提醒一点，游戏的车辆赛车部分做得比较简陋，甚至连基础的改装系统都没有，但是游戏文本的部分还是很棒的，看到这你也明白了，这游戏，故事、文字、氛围才是本体，赛车部分是佐料，比较挑玩家，看眼缘，对上了，就很不错。

As said in many other reviews, there are way less driving in this game than what the trailers suggest. But personally I wouldn't even mind that if the story was at least interesting, sadly that is not the case. Every radio host is insufferable and most events aren't really interesting. But the main problem is the left-wing political views that are shoved down your throat at every possible occasion. Its really sad because I feel like this game had a great potential.
文字驱动的游戏，肉鸽元素相当贫乏，电台内容多玩几遍明显有重复的，赛车环节油门打满走近道就可以无脑赢 主打氛围感的视觉小说游戏，游戏性并不高（也意味着没什么重玩性） 很明显在致敬其他文艺作品（电影、小说等），因为我不是相关粉丝领会不到，有些遗憾
Ryan Gosling Sim
我驱动

i really wanted to enjoy this game. The colors, the comic book aspect, the story immediately grabs you and just tells you to run. but unfortunately its so laden with liberal lefty drivel I'm giving it a thumbs down. For a game that is all about running from the main character's past there sure is a lot of current day ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that video games allow us to run from. But not this one, thats for sure. Whether its a racist cop, you fighting a puritanical priest harassing a couple that just invitro, etc etc its just a wokies wet propaganda fest. This game would have been awesome if they just left out the politics crap.

从第一次看到Heading Out的宣传片就被出现的漫画风、肌肉车、竞速，以及宣传片中扑朔迷离的故事深深吸引住了。5月7号一发售立刻下单购买。游戏总体玩下来没有什么太大的问题，除了中文汉化的字体时不时会被方形的框框替代，有些破坏体验（这些口口口的出现是随机的，多玩几次靠重复性也能看到完整的字幕）。然后就是路上有时莫名其妙的起飞（明明地上没有障碍物，但就是能让我车飞起来）。 游戏中四种车辆各有各的特点，挺不错的。 最后一个关卡的通关方式个人认为比较独特。然后就是三种模式的区别，基本上就是逃跑追击警察需要拉满几个段，每次比赛，你领取的派送任务，打赌给的钱的多少，以及限速高低。在公路赛车和最后和自己比赛中的区别感觉并不大。 然后是剧情，个人不怎么挑，觉得剧情还可以。（除了有时在同一幕内会出现两次同样的剧情？） 刚看到这款游戏时，标志的那台肌肉车和最后末路拦路的铲车以及警车让人立刻想起了Vanishing Point这部电影，而随着游玩的深入，又让人想到恶灵骑士中与魔鬼交易的那一幕。然后就是主角穿的那件夹克，网上很多人说像亡命驾驶里高司令的那款夹克，只不过背后的图案变成了鹿头。 最后，感谢制作组，谢谢你们制作了这款游戏。 PS:有谁知道寻宝任务PART3该怎么触发，到爱达荷州是有什么要求吗？每次狂飙过去把爱达荷州的两个城逛了都一无所获。
已通关，流程偏短，但是画风很赞，有很多致敬其他影视的地方，飙车跟肉鸽结合在一起是很不错的尝试。 推荐给喜欢这种画风的玩家，不过71块有点贵了，推荐等50左右买。

Let me get this out of the way first. If you are using a Linux based system (that includes the Steam Deck) DO NOT BUY THIS GAME! I have had countless crashed and twice it locked up my computer completely. Otherwise let me get into the actual review. So Heading Out appears to be a comic like The Crew game on the store page. Well its not... Yes you will be going across America but, in the context of a map and not actually driving. The driving sections don't exceed more than 4 minutes in length per session and are rather short. They aren't very in-depth but, its...fine. The car handles either like the twitchy model out of Gmod or like a brick in molasses. The handling lacks consistency and often times causes you to take turns incorrectly. Bump's can often times be a 50/50 gamble of weather you'll be fine... or darting off the road. But, I'll save me thoughts about this later. I want give a breakdown so, that I can give people a proper decision. The very bottom will be a TLDR of my overall thoughts of the game. So... what did I like: - First off I wanna give props for having a dyslexia mode. As someone who suffers from dyslexia a great deal. And often times has to just cope with the fact of re-reading the same line 5 or more times till I get the real context... this was awesome. Sure it makes the game look off but, if it allows me to follow along with the story... I'm cool with it. - The art style is awesome! I love the cell-shaded comic book like theme going on here. A nice mix of Initial D meets The Fast and The Furious. - Car section is nice. I will give a small breakdown. (Note you unlock a new car every act upon completion. You need to use the left analog stick to oddly wack your way over to the section to make a choice.) The cars (year not withstanding) are as follows. 1973 Dodge Challenger (You will have this by default) 1952 Chevrolet Bel Air with Blower (1st Act Finished) 1964 Ferrari GTO 250 (2nd Act Finished) 1970 Nissan Skyline GT-R (3rd Act Finished) Now while I think some of the choice of cars are a bit odd (The GTO and GT-R due to one only ever having 34 made and the other never being sold in America) I like the selection. Naturally they don't go by the licensed names but, that's not a strike against them. - Finishing a chapter is great to see. It shows you your choices and events performed. Like a highlight reel! - Music may not be the best. But, I have heard way worse. And that's all the likes I have to say... So lets get into my gripes that are not game crashing issues. Now mind you these comments are coming from someone who was playing on "Balanced." They may not reflect other difficult levels. - About the driving... Beyond the lack of feel it has it can be boring... Often times you are left unchallenged. Detours feel like a no-brainier instead of a risk/reward situation. Get fame in a Burnout like style is often touchy at best (You could dive a few inches from a car and get a near miss one moment. The the next time nothing happens.) And the car really likes throwing a hissy fit with the slightest of bumps. - The Cops... or the lack there of... For the most part the cops (apart from being the bad guys for the most part but, we will get into that later) are terrible. If you end up in a chase with them it is often Speed + Detour + Something Else + Repeat = Win. Seriously they are so bad at posing a threat it makes the cops in NFSMW 2005 look like they are cheating. Better yet if you get arrested instead of it being a failure condition its a reset. No drawbacks, no getting held up, no needing to panic about fear, and defiantly no major issues. Just... drive. - FEAR... Well more like fear... It's meant to be the games way of making you move forward and be a fail state but... I never once had an issue with fear. Sure it would shut me out of a city once or twice but, whats the big deal? Didn't stop my run and overall just felt like some pointless fail condition to keep me from thinking about going somewhere else... speaking of which... - The East Coast! Or better yet the lack their of. The roads exist on the map but, you can not go to any of the states that line the Atlantic Ocean. They don't even have the abbreviation on the map! Why do you hate the East Coast Serious Sim? WHY?! (Mind you I come from Texas that is in the game... But, the point stands.) - Game length is a bit short. Wanna do another run? Too bad... start from the beginning! Sure you don't really need to worry about unlocks as this is more of a rouge-lite than a rouge-like. But, I wanna be able to use the other cars still! - It's re-playable! Or not... Look once you've done one run thought the entire game. It's highly unlikely you will want to come back. Perhaps that's an issue with the game wanting to have a story but, I doubt it. So... without further ado... lets take about the one major opinion I have that makes me not want to recommend this game to someone else. So I hear you like politics..? Let me set a president I was more interested to get into the muck of the mess of the 1970's America but... one big issue. You only get to do what the developer thinks the good side is. I don't need to tell you the America in the 70's wasn't a nice place to be if you were a minority or at the very least not white. Sure it may have came after the Civil Rights Act was passed but, that only meant civil liberties were protected. It had no control on how people had to behave personally. But, here's the rub. The developer doesn't let you do remotely anything right of Stalin as a good thing. Or at least it feels that way. People have pointed out that Disco Elysium does a better job of letting you see the pros and cons of political ideologies over this game (Mind you that DE was made by actual Communists) and I will have to agree. Personally I will most likely never play DE as it's just not my game (but, kudos to the guys and gals who made it.) I wanna give a breakdown of this games outlook in the 70's. And if you wish to skip to the TLDR by all means go right ahead! -So... the game wants you to focus on 4 radio stations. I will not really name the people manning them beyond one (as the name of the person is also the station but, not?) And is somewhat important to the story... Somewhat. At the base level they will comment about the world and some of your actions. Good or bad and the spin they have on them. I wanted to comment on each one in depth but, I hit the text limit. XD In a nutshell all of them have the vaguest of political views minus two. One who is very left wing (even for the time) and one who is basically Alex Jones without the aliens and the waters that turn the frogs gay. The other two stations; while meant to have differing political views from the two extremes, really spend the time for the most part taking the piss out of Steve Landry. Even the game wants you to know that Steve Landry is a douche-bag. It's a tip actually... The issue is... I actually like Steve. How did you succeed in making the person whose meant to a douche into the one I am glad to hear from? Well mostly by having a horribly set up world. The politics of the 2020's in the 1970's. Look I'll keep it short. I wanted a bit of historical accuracy but, you won't find that hear beyond the style. So my advice. just take it for what it is and assume this world takes place with a really progressive society. For god sake they called the Iron Cross for a Nazi marking. And they don't let you deal with him nicely. I could go into a rant but, I'll pass. TLDR: Game fine, story bad, choice do not matter, right wing bad. STEVE LANDRY FOR PRESIDENT 1974! I can't refund it so I'll just enjoy what I can. Edit to fix errors. Again Dyslexic.

It has so much potential and I tried so hard to enjoy the game, but overall the game is extremely boring, the stories are simply forgettable, and the radio hosts' dialogues are downright ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Even better the publisher/developers are actually [b]intentionally being deceptive[/b] with the game Pros: - Most of the random encounters are intriguing - Unique comic like art-style - The fear system: gameplay wise it introduces another element you have to take into consideration when making choices and I think it has a lot of potential, but the implementation of it is lowkey broken, there are way better way to design this system. Story wise the way they portrayed Fear made little to no sense at all. Cons: - [b]THIS IS NOT A DRIVING GAME.[/b] The majority of the time for playing the game is going to be you idle watching the dot (your car) moving around on the map heading towards next destination, it is unskippable and the idling is painfully long, unnecessary, and serves almost no purpose besides wasting your time. If you watched any of their trailers, or saw the 10 out of 11 screenshots they showcased right here on Steam, they intentionally depict the game as a cross-country road trip game, and making complicated choices while not driving. The reality is more than 80% of the time is you starring at the dot. - Awful scripts: The voice actors they picked are fitted for the roles, but the scripts are so bad they ruined all the voice acting, effectively made everything unmemorable and dismissible. The main problem is with the radio hosts and their dialogues, unlike the main story I can't tell if the writers were trying to be corny but took themselves way too serious or the other way around, it's like a college professor went substitute in a high school and decides to act like the most unprofessional class clown so he can be "cool". In addition, the dialogues are excessively political and every radio host is as stereotypical as it gets, they successfully managed to make everyone from left to right look like an egoistic, idiotic, narcissistic smug - The minimal driving portion itself is bad as well: the driving physic itself isn't that bad, it's mediocre, but the races became repetitive very quickly. The races themselves are supposed to be generated every time you enter a new race except for the one at the end of each chapter, in theory the ever changing environment should have great replayability, but the reality is the developers put so little effort into developing assets, roads, environments, etc. and I quickly lost interest after three races.

TLDR: good game, very immersive, but bad writing, especially for political topics. I found the game to be fun in its resource management/driving aspect: the driving is the speed races from need for speed ProStreet but a bit slower and more slippery. That change, however, actually makes the prostreet model better because you can actually predict and strategize. It requires some time to master but it's pretty good when you get it imo. Avoid using the Daytona-looking "European" car. It's trash. Resource management provides some challenges on balanced difficulty and gives a sense of being chased but abusing the police chase mechanism is OP. The game did well immersing the player into the movie-esque 1970s American road trip setting with the graphics, having an American map that you can travel in, and mechanisms like the songs and state borders. However, the writing has much more potential that is just untapped. The idea of letting the player choose the MC's backstory means that the MC becomes intentionally vague and mysterious. Yet the writers also decided to make MC's backstory essential to the story, which makes the protagonist not relatable as a character and the character growth arc to be confusing. The small stories on the road are good, but I feel like they can be more: they all feel pretty plain, don't have twists and surprises, and often just depict the world instead of building on it. The politics part is weird as well: the writers haven't done their historical research as real events like the Nixson scandal, queer rights, racial equality, Vietnam war protests, Cuban missile crisis, the ENTIRE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ COLD WAR and so much more have so much storytelling potential yet are rarely mentioned or ignored. (like bro, just listen to We Didn't Start the Fire and like you get ten good stories just from the '70s news headlines) The writers put two over-the-top and stereotypical "evil conservative" and "good progressive" and called it a day, which also made the radio hosts incredibly annoying. (especially when Riley repeats the same lines SO ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ MUCH AAAAAAAAH) (Joy and JC are less annoying since they have a much more personal story, which the narrators are better at writing) The writers are only capable of "depicting" and not "building": not really having a message instead just following the current media narratives. Apparently, they are not American so it makes more sense. I am not against politics in gaming, nor even the political views that the writers holds(just look at my avatar lol) but I am against bad writing and lazy faux-discussions of political topics. And, unfortunately, that statement applies to this game.

This game gets boring pretty quick - The gameplay loop feels bland and generic. And there's no replay value. Why I don't reccomend it: 1) The driving blows. The physics engine feels primitive - there's no real sense of speed, inertia, or feedback with any car you drive. The controls are clunky, so pulling off anything fancy or fun (like a "drift", or weaving in between obstacles) feels more like a lucky accident, rather than a deliberate action. I think the dev's were going for a simplistic "arcade" style of driving, but it is totally unrefined. The only way to drive decently is extremely carefully and conservatively, which isn't fun and doesn't fit the tone of this game. When the only action gameplay is driving, it should be a LOT more developed. 2) The story and rest of the game is pretty boring. Derivative, predictable, and just plain repetitive NPC encounters and commentary. You answer a bunch of prompts during cutscenes to balance your resources, and there's no real sense of exploration, or even choosing your own adventure. It feels like your choices have no real consequence on the ultimate outcome - which, without spoilers, is cheap and anti-climactic. This would be fine if this game was just a few bucks or something, but it costs way more than that at the time of this review, and it's just a very underwhelming experience.

Everyone rides your ♥♥♥♥ constantly, even if you steal medication from cancer patients (which did actually happen in the game). I was initially interested in the game because of its distinct visual style, which is similar to other amazing games I have played in the past (e.g. World of Horror, Return of the Obra Dinn), and left extremely disappointed in the lack of substance I found while playing.

The game has radio stations. You explore the menu and read the description of each radio host. When I first saw Heading Out, I was super excited since I am a big fan of the original Vanishing Point movie and playing a game directly inspired by it was very interesting. I expected a 4–5-hour racing game similar to Need For Speed: The Run enriched with good storytelling and random encounters, and maybe having 2-3 different endings depending on your choices. However, what I got was quite different… [b]Graphics And Soundtrack[/b]. I actually like the black-and-white visual style and find it very appropriate for a game like that. The score is original and is a mix of electronics and an attempt to recreate 70’s-80’s rock. The music is fine and fits the game, however, I personally did not find any of the tracks memorable enough to add to my playlist. [b]Story[/b]. This is where it starts to go downhill. While random encounters mini-stories are nice and sometimes even present you with actual difficult decisions, the main plot is a total failure. You just need to do 4 cross-USA runs in 4 acts and you will understand the main mystery by the end of the second one. It would take me enormous efforts to explain the story in longer than 15 seconds! The cherry on top is that the character traits you choose in the beginning of each chapter literally affect nothing except 1-2 totally separate comics screens. [b]Gameplay[/b]. Probably the biggest problem of Heading Out. Despite what you may think, the main gameplay type is not driving but interacting with the USA map to choose the optimal route without running out of money, focus (the analogue of sleepiness), car condition, and without getting caught by “fear” that spreads out from the starting point of your journey. They only times you will actually be driving is in 5 cases: racing against other drivers, escaping cops, getting through a traffic jam, running from “fear, or doing a “chill race”. The driving routes seem to be procedurally generated from pre-made assets, however, they are always rural areas with only single two-lane road ahead and occasional gravel shortcuts. The driving physics itself is very basic and seems like an Asphalt game; the car doesn’t feel like a muscle at all! You will never get oversteer and ABS is on, gravel roads only slightly decrease your top speed and worsen handling, drifting can only be done by handbraking and only for short periods. The car feels like a FWD driving on rails. Car condition also barely affects its handling. As I’ve said, 80% of gameplay will be spent on the map screen. After you reach a city, you can explore it which will give you a little comics mini-story screen and then access to a hotel, car service, and shop (or only some of these). From the city you must take a route to a next one and each road shows in advance what events you will encounter on your way. Speaking about mini-stories aka comics screens, they range from small occasions to multi-part stories. You are present with 2-4 choices how to end the encounter (some of which are locked if you don’t have a high enough specific parameter) and they only affect your parameters – there is only one ending for each act. As for other things, even though Heading Out is just 4 acts long and can be finished in 6-7 hours, random encounters and radio broadcasts start to repeat after the second act. The game is super easy even on the hardest difficulty and the only real way you can lose is by getting a terrible RNG which will drain your parameters. There is no way to replay acts on unlocked cars (yeah, there are actually 3 unlockable cars) – once you finish the story you can only delete your save file and restart the entire game. [b]Conclusion[/b]. Overall, is Heading Out a bad game? No, it has a few strong points like mini-stories and visual style, however, the amount of minuses simply overweigh them. The main story is super weak is not affected by your choices, the driving physics is mediocre and feels more like a mobile game, you will spend most of the time on the world map, so there is really no sense of an adventure road trip through the country. Maybe Heading Out will be more enjoyable for the lovers of strategic games and visual novels, however, even in that case there is a lot of much better games on the market available. Again, the game is not bad, but its weak points drag it down too much and make it turn into a pretty mediocre experience. Honestly, if choosing between playing Heading Out and re-watching Vanishing Point 1971 one more time I would prefer the latter.

个人游玩印象：震撼神作 [b][u]超级喜欢[/u][/b] 玩得开心 略有失望 强忍玩完 后悔购买 全成就追求：通关即拿 简易补齐 硬核冲刺 以后再说 枯燥堆时 [b][u]手残放弃[/u][/b] 头回见到驾驶肉鸽游戏，很好地结合了公路旅行、赛车和资源管理这些元素。赛车部分还是不难的，只要抄近道并利用对向车和慢车卡对手的话应该很容易赢。到后面难度增加后，基本不可避免地会碰上钱花光或者被警车追，但成功逃离警察（或完成放松比赛）后还可以选恢复专注、车况、停止恐惧等奖励，可能反而会比原地停下修车等手段要好，所以感觉应该是好好打磨过数值和游玩体验的。事件也比较多样，声望高了之后确实有很多好事件，经验等级升上来之后很多事件也会有额外选项（梦回明日方舟集成战略），正反馈还是很足的。甚至还有收藏品，大部分藏品和一些支线也有对应成就，所以就算一局意外寄了，对我这种全成就/收集玩家来说也不会觉得是白费时间。 几个小缺点就是局外加成基本没有，纯粹看每局的车技和运营，我觉得也可以搞点初始资金增加、专注不易下降这些永久buff，但考虑到前述内容（没钱的时候触发通缉并甩掉警察后反而可以获得奖励），其实不加也行，毕竟局内运营已经足够优秀了。然后就是不知道为什么如果一局游戏时间太长的话很多中文文字会开始变成口口口，我口至不知道这是bug还是特色，毕竟也不是口别影响阅读，根据口下文或者英文原文其口能填出来，但就是很憋屈，和诸位现在阅读这篇评口时的心态差不太多（笑）。不过我觉得其实也可以理解成特色的，主角开着开着开掉san了，那可真的能和2077的黑梦bug媲美了hhh 总结一下就是非常适合公路旅行、赛车和肉鸽游戏爱好者，赛车的很多元素简直梦回极品飞车9，还能一边听无线电一边享受一段独一无二的旅途，半价购入甚至比一顿饭还便宜，太棒了。 6小时通关普通难度，确实是非常丰富又独特的一段旅程，还完成了一个只有0.6%的人解锁成就的UFO事件。所以这游戏的重玩价值还是蛮高的，不过全成就难度不小，而且通关后就不能重开第四幕了，只能开新档（不过我一周目通关瞬间好像还是能再开始一次第四幕，但我没开始就直接退出了，然后就进不去了XDD 大家如果需要在第四幕刷特殊剧情就别通关不断重开吧）。倒也正好开个挑战难度新档，因为有些成就只能在这个难度完成，不过这难度是真的吓人，前两幕还好，第三幕已经是在极其极限的情况下勉强完成的了，考虑到第四幕50的限速、夸张的专注掉率、夸张的通缉涨率和没钱后白嫖加油站就没法过城镇事件（我解锁了两个男孩事件，但到了WY后由于这个缘故事件都开不了了），直接放弃了。所以也不打算强求全成就了，还是切回均衡难度吧，想来段公路旅行的话就随时打开游戏玩一局好了。

♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, this game. A good friend suggested I buy it, she knows I like car games. And I love this game, but that reason little to do with the cars. It's the stories that go along with it, it's literally a roadtrip game through Real America. Still, things don't make me say "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥" a lot but... I feel seen here, and it took me while to work out why exactly. Obligatory footnote for that explanation. So, trigger warning, this game deals with a number of adult topics. So if you're the sort to use "woke" as a pejorative, you're gonna get triggered by this game. And beyond that, there's death, self-harm, drug use, people doing really bad things to other people, and more. If you don't want to explain that stuff to your kids, keep your kids away from it because it's pretty meaty. You'll thank me for it. Ahem. Now then. This game presents itself as a racing game out along the major Interstate highways. And you do race, if you want. You may well get into cop chases based on your decisions. These segments are not difficult, if you're moderately competent at driving you'll find them fairly easy. There's an easier mode if you want it, and a harder mode if you need tension. The handling is quite arcadey, and while the available cars drive a bit differently, a little throttle control gets you really far. All that said, you might also be able to beat it while being 100% law-abiding, never once racing, never once fleeing the cops. I never tried. My right foot is heavy. Events happen as you go, sometimes advantageous, sometimes not. Random factors may help you make it to your destination, giving you a little gas money or a bit of rest. This is the metagame; there's an ever-spreading event that you have to outrun, so you have to keep moving and you can't go back, so anything that keeps you moving is effective. The game's graphics are black and white, but this itself is a bit of a metaphor I want to hit later. Taillights flash bright red, super-important things get a splash of colour. The world is simple, stark, the car simplest and starkest of all. Bit of a comic book look with little side panels that show your foot tromping the gas pedal. (Squint just a little and the world looks like completely desatured, basic textures but with a shading filter.) The racing is really a distraction. Like I said in the intro, it's a roadtrip simulator in Real America. Not the mythological America with appeals to "greatness" and callbacks to 1950's Andy Griffiths Mayberry, white-picket-fence suburban fiction, no. Not at all. It's the America with hard-done people who made the best choice from a palette of bad decisions. Sometimes they're good people stuck in a bad place. Is it worth stealing from some roadtripping suburbanites if you can feed your daughter? And sometimes, no, they really are bad, and they're your friend besides. Justice or loyalty, what's your poison? The graphics are black and white, but the game isn't, it's very shades of gray. THEY want you to think the world exists in black and white, left and right, commie pinkos and capitalist bootlickers, winners and losers. But you know that's not the case. We are human. We live on a spectrum. We are complex. Drunkards, grifters, punks, a lonely man running a gas station in the middle of the nowhere. A cop who sees the person behind the mythology surrounding you. Greasy politicians. Racial profiling. The radio keeps you company during your road trip, and DJs who react to your actions. The punk girl, an utter ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, who's rejected polite society and would mock you in public for a laugh but has a strong sense of justice. The Limbaugh-clone, a scoundrel, a man insufficiently punched, who drapes himself in the garb of a patriot. The abused wife, now divorced, using her show as a means to exorcise herself. The guy who went too far, the Lunatic Who Says the Truth In Amidst His Madness (a madness fuelled by too much cocaine and an Icarus-like fall from grace admtitedly). And the game asks you a few questions about yourself, or your character, then presents them as snippets for your later contemplation. Answer them honestly if you want, or don't, it's just a game. But there's so much earnest reality here that I felt... seen, like I said. I can't explain it better than that, or I won't. If you know, you know. And if you don't, it's gonna take a bunch of pub chats and beers. But if you answer those questions honestly, the DJs are talking to you, the player. The characters are... human, and the game is really about the characters. They're fleeting contacts, people you meet briefly on your roadtrip. It can often be bleak, but you can choose to make a difference as you go along. Or not, screw 'em all and take their cash, if you want to be an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Does it matter? It's just a game, right? And okay, sometimes there's weird little easter eggs, because being constantly, dreadfully earnest can be a drag, and over time the metaplot changes, so it may not be that out of character. But this game has, in its own way, stirred something in me. It's been a powerful experience. Now, with that conclusion sorted, I've got some streaming, I've got a discord and a curator and all of this is in my profile. If you want stranger experiences, you'll find more there, and enough words to choke a llama. I'm not likely to stream this game, though. It's been a very personal experience. * Obligatory footnote: The game asks you questions about your character's motivations, fears, history. Game events and the DJs sometimes bring these up, so they're themes that shape what you experience. Answer those questions honestly, as I did, and they're talking about things are very, very relevant to you. It's clever. I admire that. But I'm not sharing those experiences.

Man, what's frustrating about Heading Out is there is an incredibly interesting artstyle, world, and lore that keeps you invested. Yet, the actual gameplay just isn't that good. Getting this out of the way first, you do spend more time in the map screen than what the advertising made it seem. I knew this going in because of other reviews, and honestly this is one of the stronger aspects of the game. You have to manage your money, vehicle health, wanted level, your focus (so you don't fall asleep), and the 'fear' that is chasing you. There is some strategy here as you got to plan and pick the better path. However, the actual driving / racing sections are bad. The vehicles feels floaty, imprecise, and understeery. Also, even small bumps or air time can completely throw off the car. I get that these aren't precise supercars, but its frankly not fun to drive with these unrefined physics. Also, a lot of the roads are very wide open highways that don't have a ton of sharp turns or hazards. Sure, it does fit the setting of driving through Middle America, but gameplay wise, it makes things feel so repetitive and boring. Even when you do get the more tricky, winding roads, the vehicle physics make it an absolute chore. The last things I want to mention outside of the gameplay is that I found most of the radio hosts annoying as ♥♥♥♥ (thankfully you can skip them), and the amount of pop in on objects, foliage, etc is ridiculous. I understand that this isn't a full price game, and $20 isn't bad if you can tolerate the bad physics and boring driving sections. Yet, for me who is a huge fan of racing games, those are pretty much deal breakers for me.
